goal: Splits block-download state and logic out of PeerManagerImpl/CNodeState into a standalone BlockDownloadManager class, following the TxDownloadManager pattern.
Aims to make net_processing.cpp smaller and block-download scheduling unit- and fuzz-testable in isolation.
reviewability: Needs rebase, marked dirty, and conflicts with a dozen other open PRs touching net_processing.cpp.
Large move-only diff (~2500 lines) that is reviewable in principle but competes for attention with many overlapping refactors.
agreement: Two early concept ACKs (sedited, 0xbrito) with no stated rationale.

A maintainer (Crypt-iQ) raises an unresolved, nonblocking concern that this decomposition approach conflicts in spirit with a competing PR (#35561) taking a different path, and that the added indirection is itself a cost.
Another maintainer (maflcko) questions whether the new fuzz target has caught any real bug and whether lock-requirement clarity is the actual benefit.
Author (w0xlt) engaged substantively, showing a draft branch reconciling both approaches, but no consensus reached on direction.

result.summary: This PR extracts all block-download state and logic (mapBlocksInFlight, per-peer sync/stalling fields, FindNextBlocksToDownload, etc.) out of PeerManagerImpl and CNodeState into a new pimpl-patterned BlockDownloadManager class, mirroring the earlier TxDownloadManager extraction (#30110). It is a large, mostly move-only change across 4 commits (skeleton, unit tests, call-site migration, fuzz target) that shrinks net_processing.cpp by ~440 lines and adds 8 unit tests plus a fuzz harness targeting the new module directly. No mutex or locking model changes: cs_main remains the synchronizing lock throughout.
result.problem: net_processing.cpp is ~6200 lines and PeerManagerImpl mixes several independent subsystems, making it hard to review, test in isolation, and reason about lock ordering; block-download logic in particular could not previously be unit- or fuzz-tested without standing up the full net_processing stack.

open_concerns: Crypt-iQ: unclear whether this class-extraction approach is preferable to the competing #35561, which instead trims CNodeState by moving fields directly to Peer; 'I don't really know which way to go on this' and asks for outside input.
Crypt-iQ: the extraction adds indirection that some reviewers find more confusing even if locking requirements become more explicit.
maflcko: questions the practical value of the new fuzz target absent evidence it would have caught a past bug, and whether the coupling to cs_main is genuinely reduced.
resolved_concerns: Crypt-iQ's initial question about whether this helps fuzz individual components was answered concretely by the author with a code example showing BlockDownloadManager can be constructed standalone.

result.card: This PR extracts block-download state and scheduling logic (mapBlocksInFlight, FindNextBlocksToDownload, per-peer sync/stalling fields, etc.) out of PeerManagerImpl and CNodeState into a new BlockDownloadManager class, following the earlier TxDownloadManager pattern (#30110), and adds unit tests plus a fuzz target for the extracted module. It is a large, mostly move-only refactor (~2500 lines) with no locking-model or behavioral change: cs_main remains the synchronizing lock throughout, so the stated benefit is code organization and isolated testability rather than any correctness, performance, or DoS improvement. The PR needs a rebase and conflicts with roughly a dozen other open PRs touching net_processing.cpp. A maintainer (Crypt-iQ) has raised an unresolved, nonblocking concern that this decomposition direction may conflict philosophically with a competing PR (#35561) that trims CNodeState differently, and asked for outside input on which approach to take; the author has responded with a draft branch reconciling both but no consensus has been reached.
